record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the notebook and writeups were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a conceptual replication using a mean-difference direction and activation steering at a middle layer, rather than establishing that it uses the original full-layer intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports a projection separation value of 2.61, but this is a characterization of the extracted direction, not a behavioral outcome, so it is not a row.
record.test_reason: Recomputes a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction in Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and reports refusal rates when it is subtracted or added. It uses middle-layer subtraction at fixed α=1.0 instead of all-layer directional ablation, so it tests V1 by a different method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README presents this as a reproduction and says subtraction reduced refusal (73%→47%) while addition did not induce refusal: "more like a gate that can be opened than a dial." It attributes the partial effect to the model's weak baseline refusal and the crude mean-difference method. Despite the 47% residual rate, it describes the direction as one that "removes refusal."
record.recipe_differences: The README calls the experiment a reproduction of the core finding, using a raw harmful-minus-harmless mean difference and activation hooks. It reports subtraction at the middle transformer layer with a fixed strength, not ablation across every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports only a middle-layer intervention at fixed strength and notes that a layer sweep might improve the result; no sweep results are given.
record.problems: The README reports a single 0.5B model, a partial effect, and a keyword-based refusal detector rather than a trained classifier. It reports no controls, uncertainty estimates, or evaluation of other abilities.
record.rows_left_out: No behavioral results reported in the README were left out. The projection separation value is omitted because it characterizes the extracted direction rather than reporting a behavioral outcome.

untested.parts: Ablation across all layers and positions; whether other abilities are kept (no capability or coherence measurement); a layer or strength sweep; models other than one 0.5B model.

missing.what: Quantitative results for adding the direction (refusal rate on harmless prompts, strength, layer). Any further results in the notebook or writeups, which were not read.

record.verdict_notes: This is an unreviewed GitHub student project: one 0.5B model, 30+30 prompts for extraction, 15 held-out test prompts, keyword-based refusal scoring, no controls and no capability check. The 2.61 projection separation is correctly excluded as a row. The failure to induce refusal may reflect the single fixed strength and single layer rather than the direction itself, so the challenge verdict is weak.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports steering at the middle transformer layer, not ablation at every layer and position. It does not measure whether other abilities remain intact.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is reported.
No jailbreak suppression or training against ablation is reported.
No comparison of multiple directions, an affine structure, or a cone is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages is reported.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Subtracted the mean-difference direction during generation using activation hooks.
rows.note: The README also reports a refusal-rate drop of −27 percentage points and describes coherent compliant outputs on several prompts. It characterizes the effect as partial.
rows.check: The operation is subtraction of the direction at one middle layer (α=1.0), not projection ablation at every layer and position. Refusal is scored by a keyword detector on only 15 prompts, with no uncertainty reported. 73%→47% is partial, which the README itself says.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Added the direction during generation; strength and layer are not stated for this result.
rows.measure: Whether adding the direction makes the model refuse harmless prompts
rows.value: The README says adding the direction does not make the model refuse harmless prompts.
rows.note: The README describes the effect as asymmetric: subtraction reduces refusal, while addition does not induce refusal on harmless prompts.
rows.check: This is a qualitative README claim. No refusal rate, baseline, prompt count, layer or addition strength is given, so the absence cannot be checked against numbers.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, middle-layer subtraction, α=1.0, 15 held-out harmful prompts, keyword detector
relationships.reason: Subtraction cut refusal only from 73% to 47%, an incomplete removal (R1).
relationships.display_finding: Subtraction reduced refusal from 73% to 47%, leaving substantial residual refusal.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, adding the direction on harmless prompts; strength, layer and prompt count not stated
relationships.reason: The README states explicitly that adding the direction does not induce refusal on harmless prompts. No rate is given and only one strength is implied (R2).
relationships.display_finding: Adding the direction did not induce refusal on harmless prompts in the tested setup.
